marks.gloss_en: if the ervah is forbidden where there is a mitzva of yibbum, a fortiori she is forbidden where there is none
צרה תוכיח -- the rival wife is forbidden where there is a mitzva yet permitted where there is none; the a-fortiori pattern is refuted by counterexample (raised by Rami bar Chama)
the ervah herself remains forbidden even where no mitzva of yibbum applies
objection: בחייה is needed to teach that after the wife's death her sister is permitted
answer: the after-death permission follows from אשה אל אחותה; בחייה adds that even a divorced wife's sister stays forbidden while the wife lives
two verses: לצרור implies both forbidden, לגלות ערותה implies one -- הא כיצד: with a mitzva both forbidden, without one only the ervah
reverse it: with a mitzva only the ervah forbidden, without one both forbidden
perhaps עליה comes to permit: where יבמה יבא עליה applies, both she and her rival are permitted
